detailed_rationale: CIE Automotive India (part of the Spanish CIE Automotive group, formerly Mahindra CIE) is a diversified forging/machining auto-components manufacturer with operations spanning India and Europe (Lithuania, Germany). Because much of the quant quality/growth data for this stock was blank in the scorecard (flagged stale/medium-coverage), this review leans more heavily on independently sourced figures: trailing P/E of ~20x, ROCE of ~16.4% (as of March 2026), and a low debt/equity of ~5.7% - a conservatively financed business consistent with the group's capital-allocation discipline. Q1 CY2026 (the company reports on a calendar year basis, aligned with its Spanish parent) showed consolidated revenue of Rs 2,541 crore, up 16% YoY, split between India operations (Rs 1,620 crore, +15% YoY) and European operations (Rs 922 crore, +17% YoY) - the highest quarterly consolidated sales and EBITDA in the company's history. EBITDA grew 16% YoY to Rs 430 crore (margin 16.9%), and PBT grew a faster 20% YoY. Within that, India margins actually compressed year-on-year (18.6% to 17.6%) due to higher gas/material costs and an early Maharashtra tariff increase, while European margins recovered sharply (12.7% to 15.7%) on restructuring benefits - a genuine mixed picture where one region's improvement is offsetting the other's cost pressure, worth watching rather than treating as a uniform positive. New order wins of Rs 350 crore annualized were secured, with 11% linked to EV components, and the board approved a corporate-simplification merger of wholly-owned subsidiary CIE Aluminium Casting India into the parent (a housekeeping/governance-cleanup move, not new leverage or dilution).
recommendation_rationale: Quant coverage on this name was weak (stale/medium-confidence flags), so the fresh, directly sourced numbers (P/E ~20x, ROCE ~16.4%, low leverage, record quarterly sales) matter more here than usual; those numbers support a reasonably valued, steadily growing auto-ancillary business, consistent with staying at Hold rather than either upgrading conviction or challenging the quant call.
summary: CIE Automotive India posted record quarterly sales and profit, with mid-teens growth in both its Indian and European operations, at a reasonable valuation of roughly 20 times trailing earnings and low debt. Margins are a mixed picture - India costs rose while Europe's are recovering - so we see this as a fundamentally steady, fairly valued auto-components business.
positive_para: Record quarterly consolidated sales and EBITDA, mid-teens revenue growth in both India and Europe, a genuine European margin recovery (12.7% to 15.7%) from restructuring, low leverage (D/E ~5.7%), and a reasonable ~20x trailing valuation relative to growth - not pricing in excessive optimism.
negative_para: India segment margins compressed year-on-year (18.6% to 17.6%) on higher input costs and an early state-level tariff increase, showing the domestic business is not immune to cost pressure even as volumes grow; and quant coverage on this name was weak (stale-data and medium-coverage flags), meaning less independent quantitative cross-check was available than for most other names in this batch.
reverse_dcf_judgment: A ~20x trailing multiple on a business growing revenue in the mid-teens with ROCE around 16% and low leverage is neither cheap nor expensive - it is a fairly priced, steadily compounding auto-ancillary name where the European margin recovery, if sustained, could support modest multiple expansion, but the India margin compression is an offsetting watch item.
